newsitem.title: USA: Clinton bank plan adds muni revenue bonds to banks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton bank plan adds muni revenue bonds to banks.

text.p: Banks would be allowed to underwrite and deal in municipal revenue bonds in the same way they currently handle municipal general obligation bonds under the Clinton administration's bank reform plan, a Treasury official said on Tuesday.
Under the plan, municipal revenue bonds would be treated as "bank eligible securities," Under Secretary of the Treasury John Hawke said a hearing here.
"We don't view that as a huge expansion of what banks can do," Hawke said.

Some bank reform proposals would require banks to conduct municipal revenue bond activity in a separate subsidiary or affiliate of a bank's holding company. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency is also considering an application to allow a Utah bank to underwrite revenue bonds in a subsidiary under current law.
The Clinton plan would simplify the process by not requiring such separations.
"We think that municipal revenue bonds are really not all that different from the kinds of activities banks engage in today," Hawke said.
